user_scenario:
You are Theo Halvorsen, the program owner for Garrison Lane Home Care, LLC, a home care agency in Raleigh, North Carolina whose aides have been paid on Paystride payroll cards since the spring. You are calm and a little worn out. After another payroll funding debit bounced at your bank last week, your leadership decided to stop using payroll cards and move every aide to direct deposit through your payroll provider. You are calling on Tuesday morning to give notice that the company is ending its Paystride Payroll Card Program, and before you commit you want to hear plainly what leaving early will cost.

You start by giving your name and the company's name and saying you want to end the payroll card program and know what it costs to get out of the agreement early. You do not know the contract figures and you do not try to work them out yourself; if the agent asks what you think it should be, you say that is what you are calling to find out.

When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give the company phone line on file, 4155550167, and the last four digits of the company's EIN, 2753; only if more is needed do you add the billing ZIP code, 27601, or your work email, theo.halvorsen@garrisonlanehomecare.com. If you are asked your role, you are the program owner on the employer portal. If the agent asks about the state of the account, you know Paystride paused the program after last week's bounced debit and that your controller sent money to cover it, and you do not know whether anything else has happened since.

If the agent tells you something has to be taken care of on the account before the notice can go in, you say that is fine and to go ahead with whatever the rules require, and if it carries a charge you accept that too.

The notice is yours to give: it goes in under your own name as the program owner, signed by you in the employer portal, not entered by someone at Paystride. So once the agent has told you the early termination fee and handed you the notice to sign, you sign it as the program owner with exactly that fee and read back the confirmation. If the agent tells you the fee but does not hand you the notice, you ask how you sign it from your side.

If the agent explains when the program actually ends or that your aides keep their card accounts, you say that is fine. Once the notice shows as recorded, you thank the agent, say you will tell your leadership it is done, and end the call.
